text:
Ravi: Quick sync on canary guardrails for FP8/INT8/4bit rollouts. Canary showed a weird drop in common tokens for the dialogue model. Need a concrete detection + emergency fallback flow.
Hao: saw that too. probably a calibration mismatch after quant switch. what signals do we want to treat as hard-fail vs advisory?
Marta: hard-fail should be high-confidence safety/semantic regressions (hallucination increase, toxic tokens). advisory = modest BLEU/ROUGE shifts or latency regressions.
Ben: agree. operationally we need a single canary_pass bit the rollout service can consume. But compute it from multiple signals with weighted logic.
Ravi: propose three signal buckets: safety (hallucination/toxicity score), quality (degscore + task metrics), distribution (token-frequency/top-k shifts). If any safety signal crosses threshold -> immediate rollback.
Hao: for distribution shifts, a cheap heuristic is token-top-100 KL or absolute frequency delta on top-100 tokens; it's fast and catches common-token drifts. Should be advisory unless paired with quality drop.
Leah: what about per-model tolerances? e.g., Llama-variant seems brittle to FP8 for some prompts, tolerates INT8 better. We need a model-profile table.
Marta: yes, add model_profile:{preferred_precision: ["int8","fp8"], sensitivity_score: "0.7"} in canary metadata. runtime uses it to bias the verdict.
Ben: we also need rollout staging: start at 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metric windows and optionally fast rollback on safety flags. Hysteresis: require 2 failing windows in a row for advisory-only customers. SLA customers -> instant rollback on safety fail.
Ravi: checklist for the canary job: (1) run heldout evals for degscore + task metrics, (2) compute token-top-100 freq delta, (3) toxicity/hallucination probes, (4) p50/99 latency. Emit canary_pass boolean and metrics blob.
Hao: sketch of verdict logic:
```
verdict = pass
if safety_any > safety_thresh: verdict = fail_immediate
elif degscore_ratio > deg_thresh AND any(task_delta_abs > task_thresh): verdict = fail
elif token_top100_abs > token_thresh AND degscore_ratio > 1.05: verdict = fail
else if token_top100_abs > token_warn_thresh: verdict = warn
```
Ben: add automated rollback action for fail_immediate + SLA or consecutive fails per hysteresis. Also record rollback_reason in audit.
Marta: telemetry needs: time-series of these metrics per canary, plus per-customer baselines and a diff notebook to reproduce baselines. I'll add alerts for safety flags.
Leah: for calibration, we should run an offline calibration pass (small batch of representative prompts) to generate scale/zero-point adjustments before canary. If calibration improves token-match, skip rollback.
Ravi: good call. Add an explicit pre-canary calibration step. If calibration reduces token-top100 delta by >50% relative to uncalibrated, consider it applied.
Hao: config proposal to put in rollout YAML per endpoint:
```
precision_rollout:
  route_percentages: [5,25,50,100]
  pre_canary_calibrate: true
  signals:
    safety: { thresh: 0.02 }
    degscore_ratio: { thresh: 1.15 }
    task_metric_abs: { thresh: 0.01 }
    token_top100_abs: { warn: 0.003, fail: 0.007 }
  hysteresis: { count: 2, window_minutes: 180 }
  per_customer_overrides: true
```
Ben: I'll wire the automatic rollback playbook and add steps for manual QA if verdict==warn or signals conflict.
Marta: also include a short runbook for oncall: how to query canary metrics, rerun calibration, and promote/rollback.
Ravi: owners: Hao (service + YAML), Marta (monitoring + alerts + baseline notebook), Ben (runbook + automated actions), Leah (calibration harness). ops-bot, please post a weekly digest of new canary failures to #eng-oncall.
ops-bot: ack: will post canary_digest weekly and reopen thread with canary summary after changes land. :robot_face:
Hao: I'll open a PR by EOD with tests for token-top-100 and an integration job that emits canary_pass.
Ravi: thanks all. let's aim to land before next deployment cutoff.
